title: Design continuous drain-owned landing to remove post-verifier wait
summary: Write a design note under docs/design/ for throughput review 20261104-192053-745k: make landing one continuous step owned by the drain's ordered landing queue, removing the ~499 min median wait between verifier pass and landing record. Audience is the Athena maintainer and the next throughput review.

defaults_applied.how: Note lists alternatives considered and the chosen design.
Numbers cite THROUGHPUT.md and are labeled measured or estimated.
Note is written for an outside reader.
Criteria check the note states the saving and how the next review measures it.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Existing code: docs/design/async-drain.md, docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md, docs/design/parallel-jobs.md, crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs and crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs; the design builds on these and creates none of them.
Goal: a design note only; no code is implemented here. A later change implementing it must cite review 20261104-192053-745k.
The request text is truncated; the note takes the quoted bottleneck, 470.0 min predicted saving, and 528.2 / 499.1 baseline figures as given from THROUGHPUT.md.
No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need to change for a design note.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new file under docs/design/ describes the continuous, drain-owned landing step (rebase, verify, merge, landing record in one queue slot) and explains how it removes the wait between verifier pass and landing record.
The design has an Existing code section that reuses or extends docs/design/async-drain.md, docs/design/native-pr-landing.md and crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs, saying what each already provides.

The note states the predicted saving of 470.0 minutes per landed job (baseline median 528.2, of which 499.1 is landing and rebuild, citing THROUGHPUT.md) and states how the next throughput review measures the minutes after the change landed.
The note cites review 20261104-192053-745k and says an implementing change must cite it in its request text.
The note lists alternatives considered, risks (rebase conflicts, ordering, failed landing) and an explicit rollback or failure path.
The diff changes only files under docs/design/ (plus optionally CHANGELOG.md); no athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow file changes.

out_of_scope: Implementing the landing change in crates/
